newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Arab oil exports fell 0.8 pct in 1994 - OAPEC.
newsitem.headline: Arab oil exports fell 0.8 pct in 1994 - OAPEC.

text.p: Arab states' oil exports fell 0.86 percent to 15.882 million barrels per day (bpd) in 1994 from 16.020 in 1993, figures published on Monday by the Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC) showed.
Crude exports by Arab states amounted to 12.908 million bpd in 1994 compared to 13.193 million bpd in 1993, down 2.16 percent, the Kuwait-based organisation said in its 1995 annual report.
Oil by-products exports rose 5.19 percent in 1994 to 2.974 million bpd from 2.827 million in 1993.
The organisation did not give 1995 figures.
Arab states' share of global oil exports amounted to 35.4 percent in 1994 compared to 37.1 percent, said the report.
OAPEC groups together OPEC members Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Algeria, Iraq and Libya with non-OPEC members Bahrain, Syria and Egypt.
Two other Arab exporting countries, Oman and Yemen, are also included in the OAPEC figures for Arab oil exports.
OAPEC represents more than 60 percent of the world's proven oil reserves and a quarter of crude supplies.
